HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE PRAVEER BHATNAGAR
The instant bail application has been filed under Section 439 Cr.P.C. on behalf of accused-petitioner Sunil Kumar.
The petitioner has been arrested in connection with FIR No.508/2023 registered at Police Station Kishangarh-Bas, District Kherthal- Tijara for the offence(s) under Sections 498A & 304B IPC.
2. Learned counsel for the accused-petitioner submits that a false case has been foisted against the petitioner.
Accused- petitioner has not committed the alleged crime.
There is no evidence on record that accused-petitioner subjected her wife to cruelty for demand of dowry.
He further submits that it is a clear cut case of hanging.
At the time of incident accused-petitioner was not present at the house.
The statement of witnesses recorded during investigation reveals that accused-petitioner has given Rs.17,000/- as loan to his in-laws and asked his wife to bring back the said amount.
There is no criminal antecedents of the [2024:RJ-JP:7883] (2 of 3) [CRLMB-100/2024] present accused-petitioner.
Accused -petitioner is in custody since the date of his arrest.
Trial is likely to take long time to conclude.

No fruitful purpose would be served by keeping the accused- petitioner Sunil Kumar S/O Late Kajodaram vs State Of Rajasthan (2024:Rj-Jp:7883) on 15 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/46277563/
1 behind the bars till disposal of the case.
Therefore, bail application of the accused-petitioner may be allowed.

3. Per contra, learned Public Prosecutor as well as leaned counsel appearing on behalf of complainant vehemently oppose the bail application and contend that accused-petitioner was continuously harassing the deceased and demanded Rs.1,00,000/- from deceased parents.

In the statement recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C brother of deceased -Chatar Singh and father of deceased -Sumer Singh have stated that petitioner is continuously harassing the deceased and demanded Rs.1,00,000/-.
Therefore, considering the fact that deceased died in suspicious circumstances, the bail application of the accused-petitioner may be rejected.

4. Heard and perused the material available on record.
5.

Witness Rajesh Kumar @ Raju S/o Sube Singh who is neighbour of the petitioner in the statement recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C has stated that the petitioner and his wife deceased Brijesh Kumari were quarreling and petitioner was telling his wife (deceased) that he gave some money to her parents and he want it back.
Thereafter, accused-petitioner left the house.

Similarly, the other witness Rajesh Kumar S/o Puniyaram who is also the neighbour of accused-petitioner in the statement recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C has stated that accused- petitioner has lent Rs.17,000/- to his in-laws.

Accused-petitioner [2024:RJ-JP:7883] (3 of 3)
[CRLMB-100/2024] asked his wife to talk to her family members and bring back the money lent to them.

6. Considering the arguments advanced by the counsel for the parties and looking to the overall facts and circumstances of the case and without commenting anything on the merits/demerits of the case,
I deem it just and proper to enlarge the accused- petitioner on bail.

6. Accordingly, the bail application under Section 439 Cr.P.C. is allowed and it is ordered that the accused-petitioner Sunil Kumar S/o Late Kajodaram in connection with FIR No.508/2023 registered at Police Station Kishangarh-Bas, District Kherthal- Tijara shall be enlarged on bail provided he furnishes a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- with two sureties of Rs.25,000/-
each to the satisfaction of the learned trial Judge for his appearance before the court concerned on all the dates of hearing as and when called upon to do so.
